subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should browser tool defaults move to compact goal-shaped reads and post-action change signals, or should OpenClaw keep current capped snapshots with opt-in efficient mode?
rationale: The remaining work changes model-facing browser semantics and compatibility with existing full snapshot workflows, so automation should not choose the default contract on its own.

options.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
options.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

options.title: Keep opt-in efficient mode
options.body: Retain current capped AI snapshots and configurable efficient mode, treating further compaction as targeted follow-up work only when requested.

options.title: Defer to broader compaction
options.body: Track the problem under broader context/tool-output architecture instead of changing browser-specific defaults now.

recommendation.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
recommendation.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the bundled browser plugin's public model-facing contract, and history points most strongly to steipete for that boundary.
